title: Per-row start silently degrades to whole-application start for any unrecognized `?slot=` query shape — the wider action runs without the requested slot ever being validated
detail: Only an invalid VALUE of a correctly-named `slot=` is rejected (400). A mistyped/mis-encoded param (e.g. `?ref_slot=`), a URL-encoded value, or a repeated param (first wins) yields None and silently runs the whole-application start — creating + re-arming BOTH slots, the exact side effect the per-slot feature claims to prevent ("the other slot is untouched").
recommended_fix: Reject non-empty queries that contain no parseable `slot=` param (400) instead of defaulting to the whole-app path; only a genuinely absent query should mean whole-app start. Decode the value and consider last-wins on repeats.

title: The `matched_send_at == ""` "genuine" exhaust branch is unreachable for corrected rows — the in-diff comment describes a path the find SQL no longer provides
evidence:
+              // re-tried. The comparison is a TIMESTAMPTZ compare done in
+              // SQL (r2: the string-format mix made same-day sends compare
+              // as post-correction). The contact-fallback match (no send id
+              // — the crash-mid-tick edge) is treated as genuine.
+              case row.matched_send_at == "" || row.send_is_post_correction {
+                True ->
+                  exhaust_row(
detail: The find's contact fallback is disabled once correction_cycles >= 1 (r3 W2), so a corrected row can only be found via the send-ref match, which always yields a non-empty matched_send_at (every attempt-entry writer stamps `at`). The comment's "crash-mid-tick fallback treated as genuine" path cannot reach this branch; the `||` is dead and the comment misdocuments the gate.
recommended_fix: Drop the `matched_send_at == ""` disjunct (or keep it but correct the comment) so the code and the SQL-side fallback-disabled rule tell the same story.

title: Stale-bounce stand-down on a corrected row writes no audit, Sentry, or log — the stand-down decision is indistinguishable from a silently broken webhook
evidence:
+              case row.matched_send_at == "" || row.send_is_post_correction {
+                True ->
+                  exhaust_row(
+                    db,
+                    sentry,
+                    reference_call_id,
+                    row,
+                    source,
+                    terminal_reason,
+                  )
+                False -> Nil
+              }
detail: Every other branch of this handler writes an AD-16 audit or a Sentry capture; the deliberate "redelivered pre-correction bounce" classification returns Nil with zero trace. Ops cannot distinguish a correctly stood-down stale event from a webhook event being silently swallowed (no audit row, no log line).
recommended_fix: Emit a low-noise observability signal (audit note or log line) when the stand-down decision is made, tagged as deliberate so it is not mistaken for a processing failure.
